validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION CONFIRMED, independently, twice. This row is the REX Zone 3 Capacity Enhancement Project, FERC Docket CP15-137-000: filed 2015-03-31 for authorization to build (1) three new mainline compressor stations in Pickaway and Fayette Counties, Ohio and Decatur County, Indiana, (2) additional compression at an existing station in Muskingum County, Ohio, and (3) ancillary facilities -- to add 0.8 Bcf/d of east-to-west capacity within Zone 3 (Audrain County, MO <-> Clarington, OH). FERC issued the Certificate 2016-02-25; construction commenced 2016-03-14; placed in service for the full 0.8 Bcf/d on 2017-01-06. This is a genuinely separate, sequential FERC project from P5830's Zone 3 East-to-West reversal (docket CP14-498, completed 2015-09-01) -- NOT a duplicate: East-to-West made Zone 3 bi-directional first (adding 1.2 Bcf/d e-to-w per the company's own 8-K, bringing e-to-w capacity to 1.8 Bcf/d), then this Capacity Enhancement project layered on a further 0.8 Bcf/d of compression (to 2.6 Bcf/d total), confirmed via two independent origins: (a) Tallgrass Energy Partners/GP SEC filings (the pipeline's co-owner, an SEC-regulated disclosure) and (b) EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects tracking workbook (a government database, independent of the operator), which carries this exact project under the name 'Pipeline Zone 3 Capacity Enhancement' -- an exact SegmentName match -- with Cost=$532M, Capacity=800 MMcf/d, Beg_State=OH, End_State=MO, Docket=CP15-137, all matching the sheet. CAVEAT (informational, not a concern): EIA's own project note flags a one-day-scale wrinkle -- 'REX Zone 3 reversal was mostly in service in December 2016. Small portion went in to service Jan. 6, 2017. EIA categorized all 800 Mmcf/d as completed in 2016' -- while Tallgrass's own 10-K states flatly '...placed in-service in January 2017.' GEM's StartYear1=2017 matches the company's own in-service date and the EIA note's Jan 6 2017 completion of the LAST portion, so it is the more precise answer; flagging only so a reviewer isn't surprised the EIA workbook's own 'Year In Service' column reads 2016 for the same row. CROSS-ROW LEAD filed separately for P5830 below: EIA's Additional Capacity for the Zone 3 East-to-West project (docket CP14-498) is 1200 MMcf/d (matching the company's own '1.2 Bcf/d' language), not the 1800 MMcf/d currently on P5830's Capacity cell -- 1800 appears to be the resulting TOTAL Zone 3 bi-directional capacity after that project (an aggregate/system figure), not the project's own incremental addition. Opened and read to exhaustion: the harvested wiki-citation pool's SEC exhibit (cite_note-:1-2), the EIA citation (cite_note-eia-6), and (independently, not from the harvested pool) the 2016 8-K exhibit and 2016 Form 10-K on EDGAR, plus the EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook and the REX Wikipedia article (used for leads only, not cited). Not opened: the IJGlobal asset-data/transaction pages (paywalled), the several downstreamtoday.com/rigzone/upstreamonline articles from 2005-2009 (predate this project by 6-8 years and cover REX-West/REX-East original construction, not Zone 3 Capacity Enhancement), and hydrocarbons-technology.com (predates the project).

The 1200 MMcf/d matches Tallgrass's own 2016 8-K language exactly ('created an additional 1.2 Bcf/d of east-to-west takeaway capacity'). P5830's current sheet Capacity is 1800.00 -- that appears to be the resulting TOTAL Zone 3 bi-directional capacity after the reversal (per Wikipedia's infobox and the 8-K: '...making Zone 3 of the mainline fully bi-directional with the ability to move approximately 1.8 billion cubic feet per day'), not this specific project's own incremental addition. Worth checking whether 1800 is a system/aggregate figure sitting on a project-scoped row (the same aggregate-vs-segment issue this batch's guidance flags elsewhere) -- and whether SegmentCost=$79M (USD) is owed as a fill there.
